direct_claims: This chart presents data on the mean adult height for males versus females for various countries.
The data specifically pertains to individuals born in 1996.
This means the height measurements are for men and women who were 18 years old in 2014.
The data includes information for different countries, each associated with a "World region according to OWID".
The data is sourced from the NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (2017) and is presented by Our World in Data.
The heights are measured in centimeters (cm).
The "World region according to OWID" provides a geographical context for understanding variations in height across different parts of the globe.
For example, in Afghanistan, the mean male height is 165.26 cm, while the mean female height is 155.08 cm.
Among the provided sample, Belgium has one of the highest mean male heights at 181.70 cm and mean female heights at 165.49 cm.
Conversely, Bangladesh shows lower mean heights, with males at 163.81 cm and females at 150.79 cm.

Variations in mean adult height across countries can highlight disparities in living conditions, access to adequate nutrition, and healthcare quality during childhood and adolescence. [Public Health/Socioeconomics]
